problems: VASSAL DIRECTION: the review asked the Antioch ledger to carry vassal_start/vassal_end with the suzerain as counterpart, and the Fatimid and Ayyubid dossiers to mirror the Zengid Egypt events. The schema (events.type) says the suzerain records the event and 'counterpart' is the vassal itself in both events, so those would read as the opposite relation; not written, reasons and the missing suzerain-side events are in the notes file. The orchestrator should fix one rule (or add a direction field) before the compiler reads these events.

HARIM: the review kept Harim in the Antiochene shape from 1149 to 1163. The Harem, Syria page ('fell to Muslim forces in 1149', retaken by Baldwin III in 1158) and the Battle of Inab page (Artah, Harim and 'Imm captured after 29 June 1149; 'not recovered until 1157') say otherwise; the dossiers have the 1149 loss including Harim, a 1158 regain and the 1164 loss. The two pages differ by a year on the retaking; 1158 is used. Gazetteer check: Cliopatria's Antioch 1169 shape still contains Harim's cell, and Cliopatria's Zengid 1152 and 1177 shapes hold no cell at Harim, so rendering must apply the ledger events, not the Zengid shapes alone, for the east bank.

AMANUS: dated 1204 (War of the Antiochene Succession page, 'That same year' as Renoart's rebellion), not c. 1205 as the review said; it matches armenian-kingdom-of-cilicia's 1204 gain. The 1203/11-1204 contest is kept for Leo's short entry into Antioch; the occupation 1216/2-1219 replaces the contest for the later years.
PAGE BUDGET: the repair opened 20 pages (17 cited by Antioch, 12 by Zengid) against a budget of 5 each; five of them are town pages opened for coordinates only.

Antioch 1177 shape step: no grid cell differs from the 1169 shape (gazetteer check), so it is a redrawing; the only 1177 land item on the Bohemond III page (half of Harim's villages) is recorded as a gain below the grid's resolution.
No mount write conflicts: antioch, zengid and the notes file were read back after about 12 seconds and were identical to what was written; both dossiers validate with 0 errors.
